newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: ALPINE SKIING-WIBERG LEADS AFTER FIRST SLALOM RUN.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-WIBERG LEADS AFTER FIRST SLALOM RUN.

text.p: In-form Pernilla Wiberg of Sweden led after the first run of a women's World Cup slalom on Saturday.
Wiberg, current leader of the women's overall standings, mastered the difficult Radvanje piste with a first leg time of 53.00 seconds.

The triple world and twice Olympic champion won the first of back-to-back slaloms in Semmering last weekend and finished second twice in Park City and Crans Montana in November. She also won a super-g in Lake Louise.
Local hope Urska Hrovat delighted the home crowd by posting the second fastest time of 53.32. She was bidding to repeat her 1994 slalom victory at Maribor.
Austria's defending slalom World Cup champion Elfi Eder was third on the 61-gate run held in foggy, overcast conditions in 53.92.
